comments.author: ookayokay
comments.body: This is pretty cool but what if it was a top view game? Would it not give more visibility to the player

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: I thought about that but ultimately decided that part of the fun of the anxiety is not having total visibility. But that's a good idea and I plan on making a top down replay so you can have a full view of all the chaos that just ensued

comments.author: argidev
comments.body: The motto might restrict the gameplay. Add some speed / acceleration variation to the incoming cars, otherwise what's the challenge for the players if the just KEEP THE LINE?

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: I actually thought about that exact same thing! In subsequent levels there are areas of your line that you have to use a boost and areas that you have to slow down. It definitely adds to the challenge and I think is pretty fun

comments.author: Muted-Koala1325
comments.body: Nice, it's like crossing the road in Vietnam! Looks very chill.

comments.author: Splendiforus
comments.body: Could there be multiple path options within that kind of environment that leads to unique pathing of the auto cars and more choice for the user possibly? Or which path you choose shifts the NPCs pathing. Love this work thanks!

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body:
Yes! In subsequent levels there are more unique patterns. There is also a level generator so players can make their own paths

[https://rom838.itch.io/fourway](https://rom838.itch.io/fourway)

replies.author: Splendiforus
replies.body: Would you add flying vehicles eventually as well or animals or other variants not just cars?

comments.author: TheAngelsHaveTheBox
comments.body: I've never been so stressed out in my life

comments.author: Altruistic_Series258
comments.body: Since the core loop is built around timing, have you considered layering an audible rhythm cue (like a subtle metronome or beat synced to the traffic gaps) alongside the visual timing? It'd reinforce the 'stay in time' theme, help players who react better to audio than visual cues, and could set up a nice combo/scoring system if players nail the beat consistently.

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body:
This is a great idea. I set up some procedurally generated music (it makes more sense on normal levels, not this chaotic first level) where the down beat/chord changes occur right with the intersection. But in order to get everything to hit exactly right, the tempo ends up needing to speed up/slow down partway through the level. Which kinda breaks the whole timing thing and is a little distracting. So I gotta figure that out...
Thank you for the feedback!
